findings.documented: the API key is sent as a query parameter: GET /v1/listings?api_key=IVY26-XXXXXXXXXXXX
findings.actual: the API rejects the key as a query parameter (400/401) and requires it as an X-API-Key request header instead, on every endpoint including /auth/login
findings.how_found: sent the first request exactly as documented and read the error body, which explicitly said to use the X-API-Key header
findings.impact: following the documented auth method fails on every single request; the frontend and any data-pulling script must use the header from the start

findings.documented: collection endpoints are authenticated by the API key alone; a user session (bearer token) is only needed for user-specific actions
findings.actual: GET /v1/listings (and other collection endpoints) return 401 with a bearer-token-required error unless a valid Authorization: Bearer token from /auth/login is also present, in addition to the API key
findings.how_found: called /v1/listings with only the API key header after logging in was skipped, and got a 401 explaining a bearer token was required
findings.impact: the app cannot browse listings without forcing a login first, contrary to what the docs imply about public browsing

findings.documented: the response returns a field named token, valid for 86400 seconds (24 hours), and there is no refresh flow
findings.actual: the response returns access_token and refresh_token fields (no field named token), the access token expires in 900 seconds (15 minutes), and a refresh_url pointing to /auth/refresh is included
findings.how_found: logged the raw JSON response body directly and compared field names and expires_in against the documented example
findings.impact: a naive implementation using data.token gets undefined and can never authenticate; relying on a single 24-hour login also fails after 15 minutes, so session refresh must be implemented even though the docs say it's unnecessary

findings.documented: not mentioned anywhere in the reference
findings.actual: exists and is referenced by the login response's refresh_url field; accepts a refresh_token to obtain a new access token
findings.how_found: noticed refresh_url in the raw login response and called it directly
findings.impact: without discovering this, the only way to keep a session alive past 15 minutes is repeated full logins

findings.documented: pagination uses page (1-indexed) and limit (default 20, max 200); responses are shaped { total, page, page_size, results }; to fetch every record, read total, divide by limit, and request that many pages
findings.actual: the page parameter is silently accepted but ignored — every value of page returns the same first records. The endpoint is actually paginated with offset and limit; responses are shaped { limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results }. The real maximum limit is 50, not 200
findings.how_found: requested page=1, page=2 and page=5 with identical limit and diffed the results — they were byte-for-byte identical. Then tested offset=0 vs offset=50 directly and got genuinely different records, confirming the real mechanism
findings.impact: following the documented pagination method as written can never retrieve more than the first 50 records; an early attempt at pulling the full dataset this way silently produced a dataset of only 50 unique listings duplicated many times over, which would have corrupted every downstream answer

findings.documented: example listing object does not include an is_live field at all
findings.actual: every listing record includes an is_live boolean field, which is required to answer how many listings are active
findings.how_found: inspected the full field list actually returned versus every field named in the documented example object
findings.impact: a reader following only the documented schema would not know this field exists, even though Part 2's Question 3 depends on it

findings.documented: total_listings is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns
findings.actual: the majority of projects' total_listings disagree with the actual number of retrievable listings referencing that project_id, in both directions (sometimes documented higher, sometimes lower)
findings.how_found: counted, for every project_id, how many retrieved listings actually reference it, and compared that count against each project's total_listings field
findings.impact: the insights/analytics screen cannot trust total_listings at face value; it must be computed from the listings data directly
